key_insight: Extends Concept Bottleneck Models to multimodal inputs and identifies two necessary conditions for faithful explanations: reliable concept detection and concept representations that encode only their intended semantics (no information "smuggling"). The paper proposes ways to enforce and measure these properties in multimodal CBMs.
problem_solved: Addresses the challenge that, in multimodal models, concept-based explanations can be unfaithful because concepts may be undetected or leak task-relevant or cross-concept information, undermining interpretability and trust.
method: Formalize faithfulness for multimodal CBMs via two criteria: concept detectability and representation purity (no smuggling of extraneous info).
Introduce training objectives, regularizers and evaluation metrics to enforce and quantify concept purity and accurate detection across modalities.
Build multimodal CBM architectures (modality-specific encoders → shared concept bottleneck → task head) and empirically compare faithfulness to standard baselines.
impact: Gives practitioners practical diagnostics and training tools to build interpretable multimodal systems whose concept-level explanations are more trustworthy, aiding model debugging, compliance, and human-AI collaboration.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: image + text encoders → concept bottleneck (labeled concepts) → task head, showing information flow.
Sankey or information-flow graphic that highlights 'smuggling' paths (undesired task info flowing into concept vectors) vs clean concept channels.
Bar chart comparing concept detection accuracy and concept-purity metrics for baseline vs proposed methods.
t‑SNE/UMAP visualization of concept representations showing disentangled (pure) vs entangled (smuggled) clusters.
paper_title: Towards Faithful Multimodal Concept Bottleneck Models
paper_authors: Pierre Moreau, Emeline Pineau Ferrand, Yann Choho, Benjamin Wong, Annabelle Blangero
